cites.quote: API tests use Vitest and Supertest against a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 with a fixed clock.
Vitest with jsdom and Testing Library.
Every PRD requirement has at least one test whose name starts with its ID
HMS-14 REQ-1 (S-1 AC1): a Cancelled appointment shows an enabled Book again button
The verifier skips coverage (the project has no coverage script)
Without either, database tests are skipped.
if (!detail) throw notFound(`Appointment ${formatCode('A', id)} not found`);
APT-4: two simultaneous bookings of one slot leave exactly one appointment
PAT-7: an Inactive patient cannot be booked

findings.suggested_fix: Give each Inactive case its own appointment and patch inside the test, or add a comment saying the describe block runs in order.
findings.text: The API tests share mutable state across it blocks, so they depend on order. For example, the Inactive-doctor test expects patient_status INACTIVE only because the previous test patched patient 1. Running one test alone, or in a new order, breaks it.

rubric_items.reason: Tests cover every changed path: detail GET and all four action routes for both statuses, where Book again appears, blockers, navigation and state, reason prefill and truncation, and the UTC-midnight date. S-5 AC1/AC2/AC5 now point to the existing APT tests.
Assertions check results you can see: exact status literals, HTTP codes, the exact 404 message, toEqual on the original before and after, the history event list and the field-level Inactive errors.
Error paths: unknown id 404 on the changed detail GET, and Inactive doctor and patient refusals. Edges: the 301st character, non-text or missing state, no reason, both Inactive, UTC midnight.
Vitest+Supertest with the fixed NOW clock and a pgAvailable skip for the API; Testing Library for the web. Files sit beside the existing tests. Every test name starts with HMS-14 REQ-n.
Results come from the verifier only: the test step passed with exit 0, and coverage is correctly not reported because the coverage step was skipped with exit 78.
